First let's talk about the chorus.Don't let others oppress you.  Stand up for your rights as a human being.  Similar to a famous quote "I'd rather die standing than live on my knees"
 In the 1960s, blacks had no rights and many civil movements were taking place.#BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/f9tXB45hYN

Marley seems to be referring to how the alluring traps of Christianity, and in particular the promise of an afterlife to the obedient, can distract the oppressed from the struggle for the quality of their truly precious life on earth.
#BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/QFDHguix04

By that he means: start fighting for justice now: don't just dream and pray that life begins in the future.  Sometimes we just use religion as a hiding place instead of facing our enemies now. #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/dJp0yJnmyz
